arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Data from December 1941 to December 1942 (13 months)
# Bonds = "Interest-bearing public debt outstanding" - Bonds column
# Bills and certificates of indebtedness = "public CIs and bills"

months = [
    "1941-December",
    "1942-January", 
    "1942-February",
    "1942-March",
    "1942-April",
    "1942-May",
    "1942-June",
    "1942-July",
    "1942-August",
    "1942-September",
    "1942-October",
    "1942-November",
    "1942-December"
]

# Values in millions of dollars
bonds = [40000, 42078, 44305, 44847, 45363, 48157, 48776, 51765, 53680, 54413, 57285, 57931, 64868]
bills = [2002, 2101, 2002, 1652, 3460, 3764, 5604, 6759, 8873, 10829, 11336, 12882, 17161]

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(bonds)
mean_x = sum(bonds) / n
mean_y = sum(bills) / n

# Calculate numerator and denominators
numerator = sum((bonds[i] - mean_x) * (bills[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n))
sum_sq_x = sum((bonds[i] - mean_x) ** 2 for i in range(n))
sum_sq_y = sum((bills[i] - mean_y) ** 2 for i in range(n))

denominator = math.sqrt(sum_sq_x * sum_sq_y)

r = numerator / denominator

print("Data points:")
for i in range(n):
    print(f"{months[i]}: Bonds={bonds[i]}, Bills/CI={bills[i]}")
print(f"\nMean bonds: {mean_x}")
print(f"Mean bills: {mean_y}")
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {r}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(r, 3)}")
EOF
